title: P09 – Animacy Features and the Flexibility of Pronouns
text:
Project description
This subproject investigates the mapping between morphosyntactic and semantic features of French and Spanish personal pronouns from the perspective of redundancy and deficiency. Because pronouns have minimal descriptive content, they are highly flexible expressions whose animacy features may vary. French strong pronouns, for example, generally refer to humans but can denote inanimate objects under certain conditions (Heidinger, 2019). Building on the assumption that strong and weak pronouns differ in their animacy specifications, the project examines how R and D manipulate these features to license non-canonical reference.
More broadly, it investigates how redundancy and deficiency allow core grammar to respond to cognitive pressures and the demands of anaphora resolution through flexible pronoun choice. The animacy properties of French and Spanish pronouns, particularly within prepositional phrases, reveal both the scope and limits of this flexibility. Since both languages distinguish strong and weak pronouns but differ in the availability of weak forms in prepositional phrases, they provide an ideal comparative testbed.

title: P02 – Grammatical Gender in Discourse and Grammar
text:
Project description
Subproject P02 is interested in an analysis of the discourse structural interpretation of gender features. The main focus of the subproject is the study of gender mismatches, which describe cases where grammatical gender does not agree with semantic gender (e.g., in German “das Mädchen”, where a neuter determiner is used in an expression referring to a semantically feminine girl).
The goal is to construct a detailed theory for the syntax-semantics interface of gender, enabling the explanation of gender mismatch phenomena. One central hypothesis is that gender might be described analogously to an analysis of so-called referential loci in sign languages.
Methodologically, the subproject will conduct several empirical studies to gain a solid understanding of underlying phenomena. For theory building, frameworks of dynamical semantics and DRT will be the basis.

title: P07 — Deficiency and Redundancy in Iberoromance Pronominal Systems
text:
Project description
Subproject P07 examines variation in accusative clitic doubling (ACD) and null direct objects (NDOs) within and across Spanish and Portuguese varieties. Although these languages share a substantial inventory of pronominal elements and surface configurations, they differ in striking ways that challenge unified theoretical accounts (Maddox, 2021). Many existing generalizations also require systematic empirical verification.
Building on Di Tullio et al.’s (2019) research on ACD in Rioplatense Spanish, P07 addresses key gaps in the study of null objects across Spanish varieties and clitic doubling in Portuguese. This includes the recently documented ACD system of Mineiro Brazilian Portuguese (Machado Rocha and Ramos, 2016). Through parallel experimental studies, the project will establish a closely comparable dataset for at least four varieties: Rioplatense Spanish, Peninsular Spanish, Mineiro Brazilian Portuguese, and European Portuguese. By investigating minimal contrasts among these systems, P07 aims to determine how redundancy and deficiency operate across closely related but grammatically divergent varieties.

title: P10 – Deficiency and Redundancy in Expressing Temporal Relations
text:
Project description
This subproject develops a formal semantic theory of temporal pronouns and integrates it into a broader model of temporal expressions, including temporal and quantifying adverbials, tense, and aspect. It examines the temporal specification or underspecification of features on tense morphemes and their interpretation when bound by other tense forms, intensional verbs, or temporal adverbials. By applying insights about free and bound personal pronouns from P02 and P03 to the temporal domain, the project tests whether pronominal systems share underlying principles across distinct ontological domains.
The comparative analysis includes languages with articulated tense systems, such as English and German; languages with articulated aspect systems, including Russian and other Slavic languages; and so-called tenseless languages, such as Mandarin Chinese.

title: SFB Language between Redundancy and Deficiency
text:
Language is one of our most fundamental cognitive capacities.
This Special Research Area (SFB) Network is developing a new approach to modeling the linguistic system. The starting point is the hypothesis that the cognitive core of language ability is based on logical-symbolic calculations, but is embedded in a cognitive system of stochastic nature. As an interface between the symbolic and stochastic components, grammar uses the central optimization factors of redundancy and deficiency, which can underlie linguistic operations and make it possible to process both under- and over-specified inputs.
The Network brings together the particularly strong linguistic research at the Universities of Graz, Vienna, and Salzburg and deals with uniformly defined, comprehensive empirical areas of grammar (pronouns and ellipsis). The sub-projects illuminate, classify and model these theoretically and empirically from the perspective of the concepts of redundancy and deficiency. Expected findings not only promise a deeper understanding of the basic mechanisms of the grammatical system, but also open up new perspectives for central questions in cognitive science regarding the role of language in cognition.
This Research Network is financed by the Austrian Science Fund for Special Research Areas (SFB Grant F1003).

Description
The Zero Elements cluster brings together research on structures in which linguistic material is absent, omitted, or not overtly realized. Its activities have been closely linked to the Romance cluster, reflecting substantial overlap in the empirical domains investigated by the participating projects, such as null or zero pronominal elements and ellipsis phenomena.

The Experimental Methods cluster supports the development and exchange of methodological expertise across the project network. Description
The Romance Data cluster focuses on collaborative empirical work across Romance languages and varieties. A central activity has been a data-sharing initiative designed to facilitate access to relevant empirical materials across subprojects, alongside coordinated experimental work. One concrete outcome of this collaboration is a cross-Romance experiment on null objects across eight Romance varieties, involving subprojects P01, P06, P07, and P09 and extending cooperation beyond the immediate cluster.

Description
The Corpus and Annotation cluster has produced a repository of corpora for Romance languages, covering Spanish and Italian and, to a more limited extent, Portuguese and Catalan. It functions as a network used for consultation between projects working with both custom and existing corpora. The repository provides descriptions of the individual corpora together with access links where available, creating a shared resource for corpus-based research across the project network.

title: P05 – The Role of Self in Pronominal Coreference
text:
Project description
This subproject investigates why intensified pronouns (IntPros) tend cross-linguistically to grammaticalize into reflexive anaphors. It proposes that binding operates through information-structural roles: topics bind foci. The intensifier drives this relation as a focal reflexive bound by a topic. In compositional IntPros, this structure is transparent; redundant and deficient interface operations can instead license local rather than sentential topics as binders and make interpretation of the bindee’s focus feature optional. These processes yield reflexivization at the vP and DP levels and may culminate in a grammaticalization cycle from IntPros through anaphors to reflexives, followed by renewed compositional IntPros.
Although IntPros are structurally strong pronouns, their focal reflexive component requires local topic binding, countering the usual relation between pronominal strength and binding domain. The project compares Malayalam, English, German, and BCMS, which represent different stages and configurations of this development. Its hypotheses treat binding as a central instance of redundancy and deficiency through which grammar exploits pragmatic structure to economize expressed information.

title: P06 - The (Non-)Deficiency and (Non-)Redundancy of Clitic Pronouns
text:
Project description
Focusing on clitic doubling (CD), this project investigates the relationship between agreement, clitics, and weak and strong pronouns. It hypothesizes that these forms belong to a single grammatical class but differ in structural size and in the features determining their degree of overt realization. Drawing on Kiparsky’s D-hierarchy, the project models pronominal strength through mechanisms of deficiency and redundancy, including impoverishment and rules of exponence.
It proposes that the feature responsible for repeated realization is [topic], which becomes bleached during grammaticalization. Doubling consequently develops from topic doubling in a particular position into agreement with the highest argument or generalized clitic doubling driven by syntactic locality. Languages therefore exhibit different degrees of doubling—from zero elements and agreement to clitics—depending on grammaticalization and syntactic position. The project examines how this account explains binding, reconstruction, resumption, the Person-Case Constraint, and locality and anti-locality effects associated with clitic pronouns.

title: P03 – Mismatches in Binding and Coreference
text:
Project description
Project P03 investigates two empirical domains: fake indexicals and other bound pronouns, and unbound pronouns exhibiting covariance. It examines their morphological, syntactic, and semantic properties within a model where syntax mediates between LF and PF by transferring features exhaustively or redundantly. Fake indexicals are analyzed as involving an R operation from syntax to LF, whereas unbound pronouns involve an R operation from syntax to PF. The phenomena thus form mirror images within the CRC’s R/D framework.
The project examines pronoun structure, feature distribution across grammar, mismatches between components, and possible feature sources. It tests two hypotheses: fake indexicals are syntactically bound through the genuine indexical via focus binding, while unbound pronouns are definite noun phrases that undergo ellipsis.
P03 aims to formalize redundancy/deficiency mechanisms and includes a detailed study of fake indexicals in Romance and Slavic languages. Its broad empirical and theoretical scope supports collaboration with most other CRC subprojects.

title: P08 – Fading Reference – The Pragmaticalization of Pronoun + Verb
text:
Project description
This project investigates pronoun–verb combinations (prVCs), primarily in spoken Spanish and Italian. It examines their development from content-rich predicates through partially fixed parenthetical constructions to grammaticalized discourse markers. Particular attention is paid to combinations involving verbs of cognition, communication, and perception, and to how their discourse functions depend on pronoun features, verb type and form, additional functional elements, and syntactic position.
The project analyzes how grammatical operations treat pronominal features across morphosyntax, morphophonology, and the syntax–discourse interface. Redundancy (R) may suppress or disregard referential features, while deficiency (D) may reinterpret or enrich them with context-dependent pragmatic features. By tracing these processes, the project models how flexibility at the PF and LF interfaces enables grammatical and pragmatic change and how linguistic, extralinguistic, and frequency-related factors shape the grammatical system. It contributes to the SFB’s questions on grammaticalization and pragmaticalization (Q1), their consequences at the left periphery (Q2), and pronoun feature specifications in prVCs (Q3).
